newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London steady in thin trade, await PPI.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London steady in thin trade, await PPI.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady on Friday in low volume as many participants awaited U.S. producer price(PPI)inflation figures, due at 1230 GMT.

"We've seen a bit of buying but basically today is all about the PPI," one market maker said. "Some people are looking for reasons to send this market back down and the PPI could give them the excuse they need."
U.S. producer prices for March are forecast to be unchanged after a 0.4 percent drop the previous month, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
A larger jump in the March PPI would heighten fears of rising bond yields and a near-term U.S. rate hike, dealers said.
U.S. retail sales for March, due at the same time as the PPI data, are expected to show a 0.6 percent increase after a 0.8 percent advance in February.
The Dow's two-day decline after a promising 132-point, three-day winning streak as well as a stubbornly high U.S. long bond yield also kept many players on the defensive, dealers said.

"Earlier this week a few people thought the worst might be over but the Dow has stumbled a bit the past few days," one trader said. "The only question is whether the stumble will turn into a bigger fall."

The Dow Industrials fell 23.79 points to 6,540.05 on Thursday. The June S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.55 to 763.90 by 1055 GMT while the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond stood at 7.11 percent.
Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International has little doubt that the Dow's medium-term direction is still down -- regardless of today's PPI numbers.
"Technically the Dow is looking weak. The pressure is still on the downside," Shah said. "If the Dow closes below 6,500 tonight -- look out, it's a big bear scenario."
A break below 6,500 would prompt a drop to 6,400 and then 6,200 Shah said, who is also worried about the fundamental picture for U.S. blue chips.
Shah expects investors to look beyond current first quarter earnings reports and concentrate on earnings potential -- a potential that he believes will be dented by the soaring dollar.
"People will be more forward looking and realise the impact the strong dollar will have on future overseas earnings," he said.

"If we don't get intervention from the central banks the dollar is going to keep on rising which has to have an impact on earnings." The dollar is currently trading at a three year high against the German mark and 57-month high versus the Japanese yen.

Richard Marshall, chartist at Investment Research of Cambridge Limited, is not as bearish about the Dow's near-term prospects, believing U.S. blue chips could push around 200 points higher in the coming few weeks, provided there are no nasty economic statistics or corporate earnings shocks.
"Short-term momentum indicators on the Dow are still on the oversold side," Marshall said. "It looks as though the Dow ought to rally from here."

Marshall said only a break below key support of 6,475 would trigger a further downside correction toward 6,400. A break above 6,612 would prompt a further advance up to 6,750 -- a level which Marshall believes will be difficult to punch through.
"Selling pressure will emerge at that point. But after that I'm not really looking for a major sell-off. I think the Dow will just push sideways up to the summer."
IBM was down $1/4 to $132-5/8 after press reports that British Steel had rejected proposals by "Big Blue" to take over the steel makers computing work.

British Steel said talks on the outsourcing deal, worth 350 million stg ($567.4 million), had broken down because IBM was "unable to meet our basic objectives", according to a report in the Financial Times newspaper.
Digital Equipment Corp rose $1/4 to $25-5/8 after talk that U.S. broker Salomon Brothers was positive on the stock. No one at Salomon Brothers in London was immediately available to comment.
--Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
